messages.subject: Re: seemingly basic question; cannot find the answer
parts: The problem I have with this approach is the vjust and hjust arguments behave oddly, at least to me, such that I'm not sure how to set them in order to have the labels sit nicely beside the points indicating the means. On a side-note, I'm wondering why the means in my "lab" dataset don't seem to match the means calculated by stat_summary.

Justification is generally from 0 to 1, but you can put just about anything in there and get all sorts of crazy results. For hjust, 0 means that the right hand side of your text is on the point that you specify with your data. An hjust of 1 means that the left side of your text starts at the point you specify. vjust works similarly but does it in the vertical axis (more important when your text is angled). The easiest way to understand them is to play with them one at a time and look at the result. 

Your data doesn't line up with the summary data because you told it not to by specifying a vjust. At least that's how I interpret the problem. 

#if you specify just the hjust they line up
#but you have some text overlap issues
#if you make the font smaller it should work better

b+stat_summary(fun.y=mean,geom="point",size=4,colour="blue")+ 
geom_text(data=lab,aes(x=avg.Group.1,y=avg.x,label=paste("mean:"

,round(avg.x,2))),colour="black",size=4,hjust=10)


#####
The legend seems a bit clunky to me and not really appropriate. A table with the means would make more sense IMO. 

Brandon

parts:
Hi:

You already have boxplots and points in the y-center of the graph, so it seems to me that adding text labels of the means (when the central bar in the box represents the *median*) serves more to obfuscate than clarify. Here's an alternative, which I seem to remember was posted a while back if memory serves (i.e., I've seen something like this before), but I don't have the citation at hand. You can always jiggle the y-location of the text.

lab <- data.frame(avg = aggregate(b ~ a, data = x, FUN = mean))

b <- ggplot(x, aes(a, b)) + ylim(-3.5, 3.5) +

geom_boxplot(alpha=0, colour="darkgreen", size=0.8,
                      outlier.colour='NA') +

geom_jitter(position=position_jitter(w=0.15), shape=1, col='red') +
       scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-3, 3),
                          labels = c('Mean', seq(-2, 3))) +
       geom_text(data = lab, aes(x = avg.Group.1, label = round(avg.x, 2)),
                   y = -3, colour = 'black', size = 4)

HTH,
Dennis

b + geom_text(aes(x=a, y=b, label=round(..y..,2)),
stat="summary", fun.data="mean_cl_boot")

You can mix-and-match you stats and geoms, processing the data through a
stat before plotting it with a geom. But there are limitations. You
can only go through one stat, and if you want the stat-processed data
multiple times, you are probably better off doing the summarization
outside the ggplot call (probably using plyr) and passing that already
summarized data set in to whatever geom you want.
